note: task-085. Companion to brood-variants.json, same mechanism, other side of the split atlas: how often each of the eleven team looks (retinue base + ten judged knight keeps) shows up. Owner, 2026-07-29: 'can we implement the knight family into the group... use that for materials as the enemies will change from time to time.' Nothing parses this JSON at runtime -- the compiled CVar default is the document of record, checked against this file by Scripts/art/check_brood_variants.py. task-126 added the ARCHER block: the same file now documents TWO sub-tables over one atlas -- 'variants' (Swarm.TeamVariantWeights, spearmen, atlas variants 0-10) and 'archer_variants' (Swarm.ArcherVariantWeights, atlas variants 11-23, resized from six to thirteen by task-128). Archers were fully simulated and invisible before it: with no unit-type branch in the render path they rolled a KNIGHT look, so the player could not see their own ranged line.
weight_note:
Integer weights, any scale -- mapped through the cumulative sum exactly like Swarm.BroodVariantWeights. weight 0 retires a look with no repack.

RETUNED 2026-07-30 (revision 3) into a BELL CURVE OVER BODY SIZE. Owner, after seeing the flat mix at gameplay density: "i want at most 5% of the army to be super small like this. They are outliers and not the average or part of a bell curve."

Sizes were re-measured across ALL EIGHT rotations for this. The family manifests in docs/data/art/families/*/manifest.json record ONE frame each, and they rank these looks differently and misleadingly -- do not reweight off those numbers. See measured_8rot on each entry; median mass across the eleven is 953.

v11_midguard (index 9) is the REALISTIC SMALLEST normal soldier: narrow at 34px but mass dead on the median. Below it the break is clean -- v1_narrowguard (26px, 0.86x), v7_barestance (28px, 0.88x) and v6_simplecolumn (29px, 0.93x) are the only looks under 30px wide AND under 0.95x mass, with nothing between 29 and 34. Those three are the small tail at 2 each = 4.9% combined. v8_heavycloak (1242, 1.30x) gets the same weight at the large end so BOTH tails are rare, not just the one that was complained about.

NOT judged on mass alone: v10_bracedstaff is light (904, 0.95x) but 46px wide, so it reads as a big footprint rather than a small unit. Mass alone would have wrongly demoted it.

Since task-095 this table also drives STATS (variant index -> melee stat row), so any reweight shifts the army's combat mix too. This one was checked and is very nearly combat-neutral: average retinue HP 132.7 -> 132.6, DPS 30.71 -> 31.13. Re-check if these move again -- see docs/perf/knight-subtype-binding.md.
index_note: index IS the value carried in bits 21-24 of the render int32 (SwarmRenderPack::VariantShift, shared with the enemy side -- the TeamBit says which table applies) AND the team atlas row pair (Row = index*2 + WalkFrame in SwarmSheet::Team). task-095 binds per-sub-type combat stats to exactly this index -- reordering this list without repacking BOTH the sheet and task-095's stat table swaps every knight's stats onto a different skin.

variants.look: The look that shipped before this task -- pale grey-green cloth, no weapon variety. Kept as variant 0 so a table of all-0s elsewhere in the codebase still means 'the old look', not 'no army'.
Narrow and tall, shield lowered flush, sword sheathed -- the tightest silhouette of the ten.
Lance couched and extended to one side -- the widest, most weapon-forward look.
Asymmetric brace, shield thrust out with the gap open to the edge -- left/right profiles read as different shapes.
Two-handed sword raised overhead, arms enclosing a hole above the head.
Simplified outer silhouette, shield slung on the back -- the cleanest column shape.
Bare, unadorned stance -- the plainest of the second family.
Heavy cloak, broadest mass of the ten.
Staff braced at an angle -- the most asymmetric reach in the set.
Mace raised, one enclosed hole -- the second silhouette with a real gap after v4_overhead.

archer_note: THIRTEEN archer looks in rows 22-47 of T_Team_2bit. task-126 opened this block with six archer-medieval keeps; task-128 REPLACED its contents on owner instruction 2026-07-31, looking at the shipped frame: "I want all these states as archers. The knight armor ones can be a single variant but not every." WHY: all six of task-126's looks were a steel-helmeted knight holding a bow. Against eleven steel-helmeted knights holding a spear, at a 56px cell in a near-black frame, the bow was the only difference and it is a thin dark arc -- so task-127 (size) and task-130 (contrast) were both pushing against a silhouette that was never different. Twelve hooded, cloaked and distinctly-kitted looks are. RETIRED FROM THE ATLAS by this task: archer-medieval's v1_narrowstrung, v3_loosingarm, v4_quiverreach, v5_crossbowbrace and v6_slingwhirl. Their family manifest entries stay on disk -- this is a roster change, not a deletion of evidence. v2_bowextended survives as the single knight-armored archer (table_index 1), chosen because it is the one archer look already proven to read in a shipped capture, docs/perf/evidence/task126/02-skewed-bowextended-vs-midguard.png. THE KIT IS DELIBERATE: several of these carry guns, an RPG launcher, shoulder cannons, a mounted turret, a cyborg energy bow and a mage staff. The arms-and-kit register was ruled OPEN by the owner on 2026-07-31 -- canon never banned them; the ban was an inference that got cited back as canon (see docs/data/art/families/archer-medieval/family.json's correction). index is the ATLAS variant (11-23); table_index is what the render int32's 4-bit variant field actually carries (0-12) and what position a weight occupies in Swarm.ArcherVariantWeights. The +11 offset between them is applied in SwarmRenderActor.cpp's pack loop, keyed on the squad byte's unit type -- an archer can never draw a knight row and vice versa. Sixteen is the hard ceiling on this block (four bits); thirteen is what fits with room to spare. UNLIKE the spearman table this one does NOT drive stats: archers short-circuit task-095's knight sub-type binding and read the Swarm.Archers* CVars, so reweighting here is a pure look change. Weights are FLAT at thirteen ways, deliberately -- the knight-armored look is meant to be one archer in thirteen rather than the whole line, and flat is what makes that true without a mix verdict the owner has not given yet. measured_bbox_8rot is the max content box across all 8 rotations, as pixelpipe pack measured it while assembling the sheet; every entry is inside the 56px cell, which is the gate that killed the ranged-roster family in task-085. Note two of the twelve measure WIDER than the task-128 brief's table claimed (riflecrouch and turretnest at 53 against a claimed 45) -- still inside 56, but with 3px of margin rather than 11.

archer_variants.look: Hood up, cloak closed, longbow held down at one side, fletched arrows over the far shoulder. The plainest of the twelve and the block's index 0 -- the look everything else in the block is a variation on, the same role variant 0 plays for the spearmen.
Steel helm, longbow at full extension to one side -- the widest reach in the block. THE ONE SURVIVING KNIGHT-ARMORED ARCHER.
Head-to-knee foliage ghillie cloak over the bow silhouette -- a ragged, fringed outline, the only broken-edge look in the block.
Hood up over a bone-white mask with one large hollow eye -- the highest-contrast head in the block, a bright disc where every other look is dark.
Short and broad under a hood, heavy forked beard filling the chest, a tool in each hand -- the only squat proportion in the block.
Hooded and mantled, a tall staff held vertical with a lit crystal at the top -- a vertical bar plus a bright point well above the head.
Hooded, one optic implant lit, a cyan energy bow drawn across the body -- the brightest whole-weapon silhouette in the block.
Dropped into a low crouch behind a long rifle held level -- the only crouched profile in the block, a horizontal bar low across the body.
Hooded, a launcher tube shouldered diagonally with a fat warhead clearing the head -- a thick diagonal crossing the whole silhouette.
The hooded bow look with two barrels mounted on the shoulders, one projecting each side -- the widest shoulder line in the block.
Heavy domed helm and goggles instead of a hood, twin muzzles at the shoulders, coiled cable at the hip -- the heaviest, most enclosed head.
Hooded and seated low behind a mounted turret emplacement -- a wide horizontal base under a small head, the only look with ground furniture.
No hood: black tactical suit, bare dark hair, compact carbine held two-handed at the waist -- the narrowest and darkest look in the block.
